# Faceted navigation

*Concept* · also written faceted URLs

Filters such as size, colour or price that create URL variants, which can waste crawl budget when they multiply.

**Glossary** (*Faceted navigation*): Filters on listing pages whose combinations create very many URLs, for example the same facets in a different order; Google's guide prefers keeping filter URLs from being crawled.

Narrative: the topic [Faceted navigation](../topics/faceted-navigation.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

5 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 2 shown or said at the event (2 consistent with Google docs), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Managing crawling of faceted navigation URLs](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/faceted-navigation).

- [`D1-C101`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Docs: Google's faceted navigation guide prefers prevention: disallow filter URLs in robots.txt and keep crawlable only item pages plus one unfiltered listing page, or use URL fragments, which Google generally does not crawl. rel=canonical and nofollow are weaker, slower options. `[D1-C101, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/faceted-navigation]`
- [`D1-C102`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Docs: If faceted URLs must be crawled, use the standard & separator, keep filters in a consistent order, and return a 404 when a filter combination has no results. `[D1-C102, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/faceted-navigation]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C103`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Slide, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Four ways to manage crawl budget: use HTTP cache control, have good site navigation, restrict crawlers' access to faceted navigation and action URLs, and improve or remove useless content. `[D1-C103, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C186`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Non-crawlable link markup, such as onclick links and hash pseudo-links, is common in single-page web apps, and sites that use faceted navigation should check their links for it. `[D2-C186, stage, Rebecca Yu, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C188`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: Hash-fragment links are a problem only where Google should follow them: product, category and language links need a real URL in an `<a href>`, while fragments can deliberately keep filter combinations out of the crawl, as Google's faceted navigation guide allows. `[D2-C188, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-URL-02` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not navigate with onclick handlers, javascript: URLs, routerLink without href or # pseudo-links (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-08` **MUST** · Documented: Keep faceted navigation out of the crawl with robots.txt rules or URL fragments (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-09` **SHOULD** · Documented: If facet URLs must be crawlable, use & separators, a fixed filter order and 404 for empty results (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
